P0.migration-fixtures: Freeze real v6-generated databases and sanitized supported-schema snapshots before migration optimization.
P0.relevance-fixtures: Freeze representative queries and relevance judgments; retain comparable v6 and v7 baseline measurements.
P0.full-baseline: Run the complete immutable-baseline suite and classify defects, missing dependencies, and unfinished-behavior assertions.

P1.foreground-core: Installed core-only server performs ordinary recall and bounded tools through stdio and HTTP without tasks extra.
P1.foreground-deadline: Configured 1-60 second deadline bounds all admission paths; oversized operations reject before side effects.
P1.admission-atomicity: Identity, scope, normalized arguments, exact grant, deadline and idempotency are validated before one durable admission; crash injection cannot lose admitted work.
P1.opaque-queue: Inspect actual persisted Valkey queue, logs and task context: only admitted job IDs, no credentials or bearer material.
P1.task-lifecycle: Actual MCP submit/status/list/result/cancel works and denies cross-principal/workspace access.
P1.task-reconnect: Restart plus reauthentication and renewed briefing retrieves the prior result without repeating mutation.
P1.task-recovery: Queue outage, outbox crash, duplicate delivery and expired admission preserve authorized semantics.
P1.task-cancel-retry: Cancellation before/after commit is truthful; only replay-safe operations retry; ambiguous sandbox execution never retries automatically.

P2.verify-authority: Whole-store verification detects hashes, continuity, causation, typed state, all ledgers, mappings, pointer metadata and manifest corruption.
P2.repair-candidate: Offline verified replay creates and validates a separate candidate and atomically activates it; corrupt authority is never guessed or dropped.
P2.migration-schemas: Migrate every supported legacy schema, real v6 fixture and representative snapshot including new task/capture/discovery/consolidation metadata.
P2.migration-inspect: Inspection reports disk needs, unsupported data and concrete recovery instructions before apply.
P2.rollback-reactivate: Rollback retains both database generations and post-migration v7 writes; reactivation restores those writes.
P2.durable-boundaries: Terminate at every append, migration checkpoint, candidate construction, pointer publication and projection activation boundary; no silent loss or ambiguous active storage.
P2.io-failures: Disk exhaustion, locks, permissions, corrupt candidates and interrupted replacement preserve recoverability.
P2.recovery-commands: Operator commands recover interrupted consolidation and retry failed projection jobs.

P3.isolated-convergence: An isolated write updates every enabled projection without a subsequent user call.
P3.leases-deadletters: Expired leases recover; unavailable optional providers stop retrying; stable dead letters support explicit retry.
P3.resource-lifecycle: Concurrent recall reuses generation/config resources and closes them after storage change and shutdown without races or accumulating clients.
P3.federation-access: Every requested origin needs both a live link and independent caller authorization; unlink/access changes before return deny results.
P3.federation-budget: Bounded fan-out uses one global candidate/result/token budget and deterministic ranking; identical record IDs remain distinct by origin.
P3.qdrant-local: Actual local Qdrant indexing, recall, restart and cleanup pass with the configured embedding model.
P3.qdrant-remote: Actual authenticated remote Qdrant indexing, recall, failure and restart pass.
P3.onnx: Configured actual ONNX execution produces validated embeddings and retrieval results.
P3.rerank-compress: Enabled real reranking and compression preserve citations and global bounds.
P3.degraded-lexical: Missing or disabled optional services preserve bounded lexical operation without loading disabled models.

P4.impact-edges: Generation-scoped call/import/reference edges pass integrity checks and bounded code impact traversal through the server.
P4.entity-backfill: Production extraction persists event-authoritative or rebuildable entity results with cancellation and replay safety.
P4.community-resolution: Atomic graph-generation rebuild uses public resolution in clustering and recovers interrupted activation.
P4.url-ingestion: Pinned no-redirect transport enforces type/size/address limits and atomically stores idempotent provenance-bearing chunks.
P4.sandbox-staging: Actual E2B staging proves isolation/network settings, deadline, bounded output, cleanup and nonblocking server execution.
P4.consolidation-preview: Apply binds exact source generations/selections and expiry; stale preview/source races reject under deterministic workspace locks.
P4.consolidation-identity: Deterministic source-to-target mappings preserve provenance and no duplicate semantic writes.
P4.consolidation-archive: Archive occurs only after verified target commit, touches only managed memory storage, retains sources, and resumes every partial boundary.

P5.canonical-roundtrip: Ordinary export/import preserves identity and canonical history; existing event-only bundles remain compatible.
P5.vector-roundtrip: Versioned vectors include model, dimensions, generation and checksums; compatible data roundtrips and incompatible data explicitly rebuilds.
P5.legacy-payload: include_legacy_projection serializes an actual validated payload, never a false inclusion claim.
P5.projection-validation: Malformed or canonical-state-inconsistent optional projection payloads cannot activate.

P6.exact-edit: Host captures immutable actual tool args, paths and preimages; denied edit returns exact edit_preflight remedy.
P6.receipt-binding: One-use 120s receipt binds principal, MCP and paired host sessions, workspace, exact edit and preimages; changed/replayed/expired requests deny.
P6.local-ipc: Same-user protected IPC stages receipts only from real MCP responses and consumes immediately before unchanged retry.
P6.remote-bridge: Authenticated HTTPS same-principal pairing retains bridge credentials outside model context; unavailable bridge gives recoverable denial.
P6.claude-local: Supported Claude Code performs denied edit, preflight, retry, actual edit, capture and reviewed promotion locally.
P6.claude-remote: Supported Claude Code completes the full workflow against the authenticated remote server.
P6.opencode-v1: Supported OpenCode V1 preserves session, args, results and transcript access with actual timeouts; full local and remote workflow passes.
P6.opencode-v2: Supported OpenCode V2 separately passes full local and remote workflow; installer selects compatible adapter.
P6.capture-review: Bounded provenance/idempotent candidates exclude raw transcripts by default and stay out of ordinary recall/rules until exactly authorized canonical promotion.

P7.four-strategies: Production startup runs failed-decision, pending-outcome, connection-discovery and community-refresh strategies under preserved opt-in/dry-run controls.
P7.dream-write-policy: Inferred changes become reviewable candidates; configured auto-actions use narrowly scoped audited system policy.
P7.dream-lifecycle: Per-workspace bounded nonoverlapping work yields to foreground activity, recovers restart idempotently and stops cleanly.
P7.dream-diagnostics: Health reports strategy progress, last success, failures and pending work without workspace leakage.

P8.app-host: Supported MCP App host renders populated v7 results and functioning actions for all dashboard shells.
P8.app-security: Production assets validate message source/origin, escape untrusted content, enforce payload bounds and content restrictions.
P8.text-fallback: Clients without MCP App support retain complete text responses and tool metadata names only registered URIs.

P9.transports: Stdio, loopback HTTP and authenticated reverse-proxy HTTPS pass the same authorization controls.
P9.proxy-boundary: Documented TLS, restricted forwarding/backend exposure, Host/Origin allowlists and JWT validation reject unsafe requests.
P9.quotas: Principal/workspace admission and task quotas remain bounded under concurrent clients.
P9.path-json-url: Production paths reject symlink/reparse escapes, duplicate JSON keys, oversized triggers and URL address-pinning attacks.
P9.health-redaction: Health truthfully reports capability/tasks/projection/migration/bridge/dream readiness while errors and telemetry redact credentials, sensitive content and local paths.

P10.wheel-sdist: Clean wheel and source installs pass documented workflows without editable checkout imports.
P10.profiles: Core-only and every optional profile plus meaningful combinations execute their actual capabilities.
P10.documentation: Version/install/migration/rollback/client/task/export docs and generated schemas/examples exactly match tested artifacts, including preflight args.
P10.postinstall: Published instructions alone complete briefing, recall, authorized write, outcome, resource reads and optional diagnostics.
P10.checks: Complete Python, JavaScript, Ruff, packaging and changed-v7 blocking type checks pass without weakening behavior assertions.
P10.platform-matrix: Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 pass on Windows, macOS and Linux; missing infrastructure is incomplete.
P10.lexical-performance: At 100k memories/representative 1m-event history on documented 8-core/32GB/SSD reference, warm 4-way lexical recall p95 <=500ms.
P10.hybrid-performance: Warm 4-way local hybrid recall p95 <=2s on the documented reference dataset/machine.
P10.visibility-performance: Isolated write visible lexical <=5s, specialized <=60s and dense after initial build <=5min.
P10.migration-performance: Migration through activation <=30min excluding dense rebuild on the certified reference dataset.
P10.retrieval-quality: Frozen comparable Recall@10 and nDCG@10 regress by at most 0.02 absolute.
P10.eight-hour-soak: Eight-hour mixed workload shows no accumulating workers/clients or unbounded memory growth.
P10.published-measurements: Publish cold start/model load, initial indexing, disk needs and above-target stress evidence.
P10.final-evidence: Final-commit evidence bundle identifies dependencies, test/benchmark results, client versions, RC and release artifacts with no open correctness/security/data-loss blocker.
